walkthroughs.body_html:
HL Regional Option: History of Asia & Oceania — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

HL Regional Option: History of Asia & Oceania brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with HL Regional Option: History of Asia & Oceania.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Where did the Viet Minh decisively defeat France in 1954?
options: Hanoi
Saigon
Dien Bien Phu
Hue

mcqs.q: Which 1955 conference launched the Non-Aligned Movement?
options: Bandung
Belgrade
Geneva
Manila
Wilberforce single-handedly persuaded Parliament to end slavery out of pure morality.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
A combination of moral campaigning, slave resistance and rebellions (especially Haiti and Jamaica), and the shifting economic interest of industrial capitalism.
Slavery was abolished because cotton was no longer profitable.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: Slavery was abolished because cotton was no longer profitable.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.

mcqs.q: How did medieval people explain the Black Death?
options: Most blamed God's punishment for sin or bad air (miasma); some scapegoated Jews; doctors blamed planetary alignments and imbalanced humours.
Medieval people thought it was caused by germs they couldn't see.
Medieval people knew it was spread by rats and fleas but had no way to stop it.
Slavery was abolished because cotton was no longer profitable.
